nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a profinite group and let $\hat P$ be the profinite completion of $P$ as an abstract group, that is, the inverse limit of the finite quotients $P/N$ over all normal subgroups $N$ of finite index in $P$. If the canonical map $P \to \hat P$ is surjective, then every normal subgroup of finite index in $P$ is closed in $P$.
nodes.title: Finite-index normal subgroups are closed when the completion map is onto

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a profinite group and let $\hat P$ be the profinite completion of $P$ as an abstract group, that is, the inverse limit of the finite quotients $P/N$ over all normal subgroups $N$ of finite index in $P$. If the canonical map $P \to \hat P$ is surjective, then every normal subgroup of finite index in $P$ is open in $P$.
nodes.title: Finite-index normal subgroups are open when the completion map is onto

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a profinite group and let $\hat P$ be the profinite completion of $P$ as an abstract group, that is, the inverse limit of the finite quotients $P/N$ over all normal subgroups $N$ of finite index in $P$. Then $P$ is strongly complete if and only if the canonical map $P \to \hat P$ is bijective.
nodes.title: Strongly complete profinite groups via the profinite completion

nodes.summary: A group $G$ equipped with a topology is *strongly complete* when every subgroup of finite index in $G$ is open.
nodes.title: Strongly complete group

nodes.summary: A topological group is topologically finitely generated if some finite set generates a dense abstract subgroup.
nodes.title: Topologically finitely generated group

nodes.summary: Every finite-index subgroup of a topologically finitely generated profinite group is open.
nodes.title: Nikolov–Segal strong completeness theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
